lines.trans: Rocio, wait: let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the high shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Clara, I just need the big teapot... ouch!

words.gloss: I am reaching for; looking for

lines.trans: Rocio! Grab my arm! Sit right down on this chair: don't stand up!
Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes?
My toes move fine, nothing broken: just a sharp pull on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap ice in a clean cloth.
No, no, Clara! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty tarts left to finish!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: If you stand on a swollen ankle today, you won't walk for two weeks!
And who bakes tomorrow's fresh bread and lemon cream if I am sitting down?!
Look around this house, Rocio: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait a moment... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
Rocio, wait: let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the high shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Clara, I just need the big teapot... ouch!

words.gloss: I am reaching for; looking for

Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes?
My toes move fine, nothing broken: just a sharp pull on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap ice in a clean cloth.
No, no, Clara! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty tarts left to finish!

lines.trans: If you stand on a swollen ankle today, you won't walk for two weeks!
And who bakes tomorrow's fresh bread and lemon cream if I am sitting down?!
Look around this house, Rocio: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait a moment... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
Rocio, wait: let me hold that wooden stool while you reach the high shelf!
I climb this little stool ten times a week, Clara, I just need the big teapot... ouch!

Ooh... my right shoe slipped on the bottom rung when I stepped down!
Let me slip your shoe off gently. Can you wiggle your toes?
My toes move fine, nothing broken: just a sharp pull on the outside of my ankle.
Keep your foot up on this second chair while I wrap ice in a clean cloth.
No, no, Clara! Tomorrow is Wednesday! I have lentil soup and twenty tarts left to finish!

words.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

lines.trans: If you stand on a swollen ankle today, you won't walk for two weeks!
And who bakes tomorrow's fresh bread and lemon cream if I am sitting down?!
Look around this house, Rocio: you have six pairs of hands and one loud voice!
Wait a moment... you want me to sit on a cushion and boss everyone around?!
Good night!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.text: La cocina está abajo.
examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

agarrar.gloss: to grip; to stick; to take hold

meanings.en: to grip; to stick; to take hold
meanings.note: Said of paint or glue adhering to dry wood, as well as gripping with the hand.

examples.text: La pintura nueva agarra muy bien sobre madera seca.
examples.trans: Fresh paint sticks very well on dry wood.

examples.text: Agarra fuerte el otro extremo de la mesa.
examples.trans: Grip the other end of the table firmly.

meanings.note: Ahora mismo means 'right now'.

examples.text: Voy para allá ahora mismo.
examples.trans: I am heading there right now.

examples.text: Ahora tenemos cuatro mesas libres.
examples.trans: Now we have four free tables.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Mi hermano es muy alto.
examples.trans: My brother is very tall.

examples.text: Las ventanas de esta casa son altas.
examples.trans: The windows in this house are tall.

apoyar.gloss: to lean; to rest; to support

meanings.en: to lean; to rest; to support
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb; apoyar algo contra la pared means 'to lean something against the wall'.

examples.text: Apoya la escalera con cuidado contra el ladrillo.
examples.trans: Lean the ladder carefully against the brick.

examples.text: Apoyamos las sillas dobladas debajo del arco.
examples.trans: We lean the folded chairs under the arch.

meanings.note: Opposite of abajo.

examples.text: Las habitaciones están arriba.
examples.trans: The bedrooms are upstairs.

examples.text: Mira arriba hacia el balcón.
examples.trans: Look up toward the balcony.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise, sympathy, or mild dismay.

examples.text: ¡Ay, casi olvido el paraguas!
examples.trans: Oh, I nearly forgot my umbrella!

examples.text: ¡Ay, qué susto me has dado!
examples.trans: Goodness, what a fright you gave me!

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Diminutive of banco (with c -> qu spelling change).

examples.text: Sujeta firme el banquito antes de subir al estante.
examples.trans: Hold the step stool steady before climbing to the shelf.

examples.text: Pusimos un banquito bajo de madera junto al limonero.
examples.trans: We put a low wooden bench beside the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Llevar algo en brazos means 'to carry something in one's arms'.

examples.text: Llevo dos cestas llenas en los brazos.
examples.trans: I am carrying two full baskets in my arms.

examples.text: Descansa los brazos después de subir las cajas.
examples.trans: Rest your arms after carrying up the boxes.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.text: Busco la puerta azul.
examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Camino veinte minutos hasta el centro.
examples.trans: I walk twenty minutes to the city centre.

examples.text: Caminamos despacio por el puente.
examples.trans: We walk slowly across the bridge.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.text: Mi casa está cerca del mar.
examples.trans: My house is near the sea.

examples.text: Hoy como en casa.
examples.trans: Today I'm having lunch at home.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

meanings.note: Drops the written accent in the plural: cojines.

examples.text: Pusimos cojines blancos en los bancos del patio.
examples.trans: We placed white cushions on the courtyard benches.

examples.text: Apoya la espalda contra este cojín blando.
examples.trans: Rest your back against this soft cushion.

meanings.note: Crema de limón is smooth lemon curd/custard filling for tarts.

examples.text: La crema de limón espesa despacio a fuego suave.
examples.trans: The lemon curd thickens slowly over gentle heat.

examples.text: Deja enfriar la crema antes de rellenar las tartas.
examples.trans: Let the cream cool before filling the tarts.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Covers both fingers (dedos de la mano) and toes (dedos del pie).

examples.text: Sujeta la hoja antigua con dos dedos limpios.
examples.trans: Hold the old sheet with two clean fingers.

examples.text: Los dedos vuelan suaves sobre las teclas blancas.
examples.trans: Her fingers glide gently over the white keys.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Opposite of izquierdo; el derecho means 'the right one'.

examples.text: El cajón derecho guarda las cucharas limpias de postre.
examples.trans: The right-hand drawer holds the clean dessert spoons.

examples.text: Mantén el cuadro bien derecho sobre la pared blanca.
examples.trans: Keep the picture nice and straight on the white wall.

meanings.note: Everyday single-word opposite of rápido.

examples.text: Camina despacio por las escaleras.
examples.trans: Walk slowly on the stairs.

examples.text: Gira la rueda muy despacio.
examples.trans: Turn the wheel very slowly.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para empezar.
examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.

examples.text: Su recepción merece un diez.
examples.trans: Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Stem-changing o -> ue in present (envuelvo); irregular participle envuelto.

examples.text: Clara envuelve el pan caliente en un paño de lino.
examples.trans: Clara wraps the warm bread in a linen cloth.

examples.text: Envolvimos los vasos de cristal con papel grueso.
examples.trans: We wrapped the glass tumblers in thick paper.

meanings.note: Single step of a staircase (plural: escalones).

examples.text: Cuidado con el escalón al entrar.
examples.trans: Mind the step as you go in.

examples.text: El gato duerme en el primer escalón.
examples.trans: The cat sleeps on the first step.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.text: El estante está aquí.
examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.text: El desayuno ya está listo.
examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.

examples.text: ¿Dónde están las llaves de latón?
examples.trans: Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

faltar.gloss: to be missing; to remain until (time)

meanings.en: to be missing; to remain until (time)
meanings.note: Faltan cinco para las doce = it is five to twelve.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to noon.

examples.text: En esta mesa falta una cucharilla.
examples.trans: A teaspoon is missing at this table.

meanings.note: Por fuera = on the outside.

examples.text: Hace frío fuera esta mañana.
examples.trans: It is cold outside this morning.

examples.text: La maleta es azul por fuera.
examples.trans: The suitcase is blue on the outside.

meanings.note: Also used adverbially (llover/discutir fuerte).

examples.text: Mi padre es muy fuerte.
examples.trans: My father is very strong.

examples.text: Hoy hace un viento fuerte.
examples.trans: There is a strong wind today.

grande.gloss: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)

meanings.en: big; large; great (gran before sg noun)
meanings.note: Shortens to gran before any singular noun (un gran libro, una gran idea).

examples.text: Tenemos una mesa grande en el patio.
examples.trans: We have a big table in the courtyard.

examples.text: Es una gran noticia para todos.
examples.trans: It is great news for everyone.

meanings.note: Silent h-; diphthong ie- pronounced [ʝe].

examples.text: Pon un poco de hielo envuelto sobre el tobillo.
examples.trans: Put a little wrapped ice on your ankle.

examples.text: En verano servimos agua fresca con hielo y limón.
examples.trans: In summer we serve cool water with ice and lemon.

meanings.note: Participle of hinchar ('to swell') used as a 4-form adjective.

examples.text: La madera húmeda estaba hinchada tras tanta lluvia.
examples.trans: The damp wood was swollen after so much rain.

examples.text: Mantén en alto el pie hinchado toda la noche.
examples.trans: Keep your swollen foot elevated all night.

meanings.note: Built from horno (oven).

examples.text: La panadera hornea bizcochos cada viernes.
examples.trans: The baker bakes sponge cakes every Friday.

examples.text: Esta mañana horneamos pan crujiente.
examples.trans: This morning we baked crusty bread.

meanings.note: El día de hoy = today.

examples.text: Hoy es viernes por fin.
examples.trans: Today is finally Friday.

examples.text: ¿Qué desayunamos hoy?
examples.trans: What are we having for breakfast today?

meanings.note: Ir a + infinitive expresses near future ('going to do').

examples.text: Voy a abrir la puerta ahora.
examples.trans: I am going to open the door now.

examples.text: ¿Cómo va todo esta mañana?
examples.trans: How is everything going this morning?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Usually plural (lentejas) when referring to lentil soup or stew.

examples.text: Una sopa caliente de lentejas reconforta en invierno.
examples.trans: A hot lentil soup is comforting in winter.

examples.text: Cocemos las lentejas a fuego lento con verduras frescas.
examples.trans: We simmer the lentils slowly with fresh vegetables.

levantar.gloss: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)

meanings.en: to lift; to raise; to get up (levantarse)
meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Levanta esa esquina de la alfombra.
examples.trans: Lift that corner of the rug.

examples.text: Nos levantamos a las seis y media.
examples.trans: We get up at six thirty.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: La habitación ya está limpia.
examples.trans: The room is already clean.

examples.text: Necesito una toalla limpia.
examples.trans: I need a clean towel.

meanings.note: Plural limones.

examples.text: Un té con limón, por favor.
examples.trans: A tea with lemon, please.

examples.text: En el patio hay un limonero lleno de limones.
examples.trans: In the courtyard there's a lemon tree full of lemons.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.text: La mesa es de madera.
examples.trans: The table is made of wood.

examples.text: Me gusta el olor de la madera.
examples.trans: I like the smell of wood.

meanings.note: Everyday synonym of enviar.

examples.text: Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
examples.trans: I will send you a message when I arrive.

examples.text: Mi primo me mandó naranjas de Valencia.
examples.trans: My cousin sent me oranges from Valencia.

meanings.note: Feminine despite ending in -o: la mano, las manos; a mano derecha = on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Gira después de la farmacia a mano derecha.
examples.trans: Turn past the pharmacy on your right-hand side.

examples.text: Tengo las manos limpias.
examples.trans: My hands are clean.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.

examples.text: ¡Hasta mañana a las ocho!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Links two simultaneous actions.

examples.text: Espera aquí mientras abro la puerta.
examples.trans: Wait here while I open the door.

examples.text: Preparo el té mientras sale el pan.
examples.trans: I make the tea while the bread comes out.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.text: Un momento, ahora vuelvo.
examples.trans: One moment, I'll be right back.

examples.text: En este momento no puedo hablar.
examples.trans: I can't talk right now.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: muevo).

examples.text: Movemos la mesa bajo la sombra.
examples.trans: We move the table into the shade.

examples.text: El viento suave movió las hojas.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze stirred the leaves.

meanings.note: Todo el mundo literally 'all the world' means 'everyone'.

examples.text: El mundo está aquí.
examples.trans: The world is here.

examples.text: Vemos los mundos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the worlds from the door.

nada.gloss: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)

meanings.en: nothing; not at all (de nada = you're welcome)
meanings.note: No pasa nada = no problem; nada de... = no ... at all.

examples.text: Tranquilo, no pasa nada.
examples.trans: Easy now, there is no problem at all.

examples.text: No queda nada de mantequilla.
examples.trans: There is no butter left at all.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: Compro pan todas las mañanas.
examples.trans: I buy bread every morning.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas el pan, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the bread, please?

meanings.note: Plural los pares (dos pares de gafas = two pairs of glasses).

examples.text: El par está aquí.
examples.trans: The pair is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pares desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pairs from the door.

meanings.note: Kitchen or polishing cloth.

examples.text: El paño está aquí.
examples.trans: The cloth is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paños desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cloths from the door.

meanings.note: Estar de pie means 'to stand / be standing'; ir a pie means 'to walk'.

examples.text: Después de seis horas de pie agradezco una silla.
examples.trans: After six hours on my feet I welcome a chair.

examples.text: Descansa los pies sobre este taburete bajo de madera.
examples.trans: Rest your feet on this low wooden stool.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

quitar.gloss: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)

meanings.en: to remove; to wipe off; to take off (quitarse)
meanings.note: Quítate el abrigo = take off your coat; quitar el polvo = dust.

examples.text: Quito el polvo del tablero de madera.
examples.trans: I wipe the dust off the wooden board.

examples.text: Quítate el abrigo mojado y pasa.
examples.trans: Take off your wet coat and come in.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.text: ¿Quién ha dejado este sobre aquí?
examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.text: ¿De quién es esta maleta azul?
examples.trans: Whose blue suitcase is this?

meanings.note: Often used reflexively (resbalarse) when a foot or shoe slips.

examples.text: Ten cuidado para no resbalar en el escalón mojado.
examples.trans: Be careful not to slip on the wet step.

examples.text: La cuchara se resbaló dentro del cuenco de cristal.
examples.trans: The spoon slipped inside the glass bowl.

meanings.note: Regular verb with irregular past participle roto.

examples.text: Ten cuidado de no romper la taza.
examples.trans: Be careful not to break the cup.

examples.text: El viento rompió una rama seca.
examples.trans: The wind snapped a dry branch.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.text: Es una pieza segunda.
examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Las seis = six o'clock.

examples.text: Me despierto a las seis y media.
examples.trans: I wake up at six thirty.

examples.text: Tengo seis limones en la cesta.
examples.trans: I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Fin de semana = weekend; la semana que viene = next week.

examples.text: Voy al gimnasio tres veces por semana.
examples.trans: I go to the gym three times a week.

examples.text: La semana que viene estoy de vacaciones.
examples.trans: Next week I'm on holiday.

meanings.note: Estar sentado = to be sitting.

examples.text: Es una pieza sentada.
examples.trans: It is a seated piece.

examples.text: Esperen: ¿quién está sentado a diez metros en nuestro patio ahora mismo?
examples.trans: Wait—who is sitting ten metres away in our courtyard right now?

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: me siento, ¡siéntese!).

examples.text: Siéntese junto a la ventana, por favor.
examples.trans: Sit down by the window, please.

examples.text: Nos sentamos bajo el limonero.
examples.trans: We sit down under the lemon tree.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.

examples.text: Esa maleta azul es mía.
examples.trans: That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.text: Avísame si necesitas otra manta.
examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Wooden or folding chair.

examples.text: ¿Está libre esta silla?
examples.trans: Is this chair free?

examples.text: Necesitamos dos sillas más.
examples.trans: We need two more chairs.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.text: Solo necesito cinco minutos más.
examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.

examples.text: Queda una sola habitación libre.
examples.trans: Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Hecho una sopa = soaked through.

examples.text: La sopa está aquí.
examples.trans: The soup is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sopas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the soups from the door.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Sujeta bien la linterna, por favor.
examples.trans: Hold the flashlight steady, please.

examples.text: Sujetó la nota con un clip metálico.
examples.trans: She clipped the note with a metal paperclip.

meanings.note: Backless wooden stool used in kitchens, workshops, or cafés.

examples.text: Acerca ese taburete alto junto a la encimera, por favor.
examples.trans: Bring that tall stool over by the counter, please.

examples.text: Guardamos dos taburetes de madera debajo de la barra.
examples.trans: We keep two wooden stools underneath the counter.

meanings.note: Usual word in Spain for a sweet tart or birthday cake.

examples.text: Hay tarta de chocolate para el postre.
examples.trans: There is chocolate cake for dessert.

examples.text: Mi abuela hace una tarta de manzana riquísima.
examples.trans: My grandmother makes a delicious apple tart.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Built from té (tea).

examples.text: La tetera está aquí.
examples.trans: The teapot is here.

examples.text: Vemos las teteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teapots from the door.

meanings.note: In Spain, pan tierno is freshly baked bread with a soft crumb.

examples.text: Las hogazas salen tiernas por dentro y muy crujientes.
examples.trans: The loaves come out soft inside and very crusty.

examples.text: Las zanahorias tiernas dan un dulzor suave al caldo.
examples.trans: Tender young carrots give a gentle sweetness to the broth.

meanings.note: From tirar ('to pull'); un tirón en el tobillo means 'a strain / pull in the ankle'.

examples.text: Noté un pequeño tirón al bajar del último escalón.
examples.trans: I felt a slight pull stepping off the bottom stair.

examples.text: Abre el cajón despacio y sin dar tirones bruscos.
examples.trans: Open the drawer slowly without giving sharp tugs.

meanings.note: Everyday anatomical noun.

examples.text: Envuelve el tobillo con un paño frío diez minutos.
examples.trans: Wrap your ankle with a cold cloth for ten minutes.

examples.text: Con buen calzado caminas seguro sin torcerte los tobillos.
examples.trans: With sturdy shoes you walk safely without twisting your ankles.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Natural exclamation of effort, relief, or sudden heat/rain.

examples.text: ¡Uf, cuánto pesa esta contraventana de madera maciza!
examples.trans: Whew, how heavy this solid wood shutter is!

examples.text: ¡Uf, entramos en el pasillo justo antes del chaparrón!
examples.trans: Phew, we got into the hallway right before the downpour!

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Mide exactamente veinte milímetros.
examples.trans: It measures exactly twenty millimetres.

examples.text: Son las once y veinte.
examples.trans: It is eleven twenty.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.text: Te llamo otra vez mañana.
examples.trans: I'll call you again tomorrow.

examples.text: Voy a la playa una vez a la semana.
examples.trans: I go to the beach once a week.

meanings.note: Plural las voces; en voz baja = in a low voice.

examples.text: La voz está aquí.
examples.trans: The voice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las voces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the voices from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: Plural los zapatos.

examples.text: El zapato está aquí.
examples.trans: The shoe is here.

examples.text: Vemos los zapatos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shoes from the door.
